questions.knowledge_point: Using the Particular Solution of a Logistic Growth Initial Value Problem to Make Predictions
questions.problem: The growth rate of the hedgehog population $P(t)$ in a certain forest is jointly proportional to the hedgehog population at time $t,$ measured in years, and the difference between the forest's carrying capacity and the hedgehog population. The constant of proportionality is $0.000\,005$ and the carrying capacity is $50\,000.$ How many hedgehogs will there be in the forest after $20$ years given that there were $12\,500$ hedgehogs initially? Round your answer to the nearest integer.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the hedgehog population's growth rate is *jointly* proportional to the hedgehog population at time $t$ and the difference between the carrying capacity and the hedgehog population, the hedgehog population follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.000\,005,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=50\,000.$ Therefore, the hedgehog population growth is given by the equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.000\,005P(50\,000-P).
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{50\,000}{1+C{e}^{-(50\,000\cdot 0.000\,005)t}}=\frac{50\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.25t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=12\,500$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0) & =12\,500 \\ \frac{50\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.25(0)}} & =12\,500 \\ 1+C & =4 \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{50\,000}{1+3{e}^{-0.25\cdot t}}
$$

Finally, we substitute $t=20$ into the expression for $P(t),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(20) & =\frac{50\,000}{1+3{e}^{-0.25\cdot 20}} \\  & ≈49\,009.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The growth rate of the hamster population $P(t)$ in the Pets' Corner pet shop is jointly proportional to the hamster population at time $t,$ measured in years, and the difference between Pets' Corner's carrying capacity and the hamster population. If the constant of proportionality is $0.002\,5$ and the carrying capacity is $100,$ then find an expression for the hamster population after $t$ years, given that there were $5$ hamsters in the pets' corner initially.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the hamster population's growth rate is *jointly* proportional to the hamster population at time $t$ and the difference between the carrying capacity and the hamster population, the hamster population follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality $k=0.002\,5,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=100.$ Therefore, the hamster population growth is given by the equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.002\,5P(100-P).
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{100}{1+C{e}^{-(100\cdot 0.002\,5)t}}=\frac{100}{1+C{e}^{-0.25t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=5$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{100}{1+C{e}^{-0.25\cdot 0}} & =5 \\ 1+C & =\frac{100}{5} \\ C & =20-1 \\  & =19.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{100}{1+19{e}^{-0.25t}}.
$$

questions.problem:
The population $P(t)$ of insects in a greenhouse follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.6P-0.002{P}^{2},
$$

where $t$ is the time, measured in days. If there were $40$ insects in the greenhouse initially, how many insects were in the greenhouse after $3$ days? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

After $3$ days, approximately
{{field-1}} insects were in the greenhouse.
questions.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity. 

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}},
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

We start by factoring the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dP}{dt} & =0.6P-0.002{P}^{2} \\  & =0.002P(300-P).\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the constant of proportionality is $k=0.002,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=300.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
P(t)=\frac{300}{1+C{e}^{-(300\cdot 0.002)t}}=\frac{300}{1+C{e}^{-0.6t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=40$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{300}{1+C{e}^{-0.6(0)}} & =40 \\ 1+C & =\frac{300}{40} \\ C & =7.5-1 \\  & =6.5.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{300}{1+6.5{e}^{-0.6t}}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $t=3$ into the expression for $P(t),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3) & =\frac{300}{1+6.5{e}^{-0.6(3)}} \\  & ≈145.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, after $3$ days, approximately $145$ insects were in the greenhouse.

questions.problem:
The population $P(t)$ of customers using a new ride-share service in a city follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.18P-0.000\,12{P}^{2},
$$

where $t$ is the time, measured in months. If there were $900$ customers using the service initially, how many customers were using the service after $8$ months? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

After $8$ months, approximately
{{field-1}} customers were using the service.
questions.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity. 

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}},
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

We start by factoring the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dP}{dt} & =0.18P-0.000\,12{P}^{2} \\  & =0.000\,12P(1500-P).\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the constant of proportionality is $k=0.00012,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=1500.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
P(t)=\frac{1500}{1+C{e}^{-(1500\cdot 0.000\,12)t}}=\frac{1500}{1+C{e}^{-0.18t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=900$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1500}{1+C{e}^{-0.18(0)}} & =900 \\ 1+C & =\frac{1500}{900} \\ C & =\frac{5}{3}-1 \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{1500}{1+\frac{2}{3}{e}^{-0.18t}}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $t=8$ into the expression for $P(t),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(8) & =\frac{1500}{1+\frac{2}{3}{e}^{-0.18(8)}} \\  & ≈1295.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, after $8$ months, approximately $1295$ customers were using the service.
